targetText: In what relation do the Communists stand to the proletarians as a whole?
summary: Communists do not form a separate party opposed to workers; they represent the interests of the entire working class.
context: The Manifesto emphasizes working-class unity across different industries and nationalities.

targetText: single sentence: Abolition of private property.
summary: Communism seeks to abolish private ownership of productive assets (factories, land, mines), not personal possessions.
context: Marx clarifies the difference between personal items (clothes, homes) and private capital used to exploit labor.

targetText:
Does it require deep intuition to comprehend that man's ideas, views,
and conception, in one word, man's consciousness, changes with every change
in the conditions of his material existence, in his social relations and
in his social life?

What else does the history of ideas prove, than that intellectual
production changes its character in proportion as material production is
changed? The ruling ideas of each age have ever been the ideas of its ruling
class.
summary: Refutation of philosophical idealism: human consciousness and ruling ideas are shaped by material production and class power.
explanation: Against idealist philosophers who claim that eternal ideas drive history, Marx and Engels demonstrate that ideas evolve alongside material social relations, and that the dominant ideology of any epoch reflects the material interests of its ruling class.
